data.name: Santan
data.gender_notes: Santan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Santan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'santana' which means 'that which is eternal, endless and continuous'. It is also used to describe the unending cycle of birth, death and rebirth. The name Santan carries the meaning “The eternal and endless one” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Santan usually hope their child will grow to embody the eternal and endless one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Santan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, the name Santan holds a deep sense of reverence and respect for its-carriers. It is often given to children born in families where the previous generation had produced several offsprings, making the child a part of an ever-expanding family tree. This naming convention reflects the importance of family, continuity and the cyclical nature of life in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Santan embodies the eternal and unending nature of the soul. It symbolizes the concept of reincarnation and the continued evolution and growth of the soul through many lifetimes. The name also reminds the bearer of his/her duty to live a virtuous life and contribute positively to the world in order to attain the ultimate goal of moksha or spiritual liberation.
